questions.question: Which of the following Articles deals with the citizenship of people of Indian origin residing outside India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 8** of the Indian Constitution deals specifically with the **citizenship of people of Indian origin residing outside India**.
 
• It provides that a person who is of Indian origin and residing outside India, but born outside India, can register themselves as an Indian citizen with the diplomatic or consular representatives of India in the country where they currently reside.
 
• This article ensures that individuals of Indian descent, who have migrated to other countries but wish to retain their ties with India, can acquire Indian citizenship under certain conditions.
 
• This provision aims to maintain a connection with the Indian diaspora and give them the opportunity to participate in India's socio-political framework. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Article 8** complements other articles in Part II of the Constitution that deal with citizenship by addressing unique cases of individuals born outside India but having Indian origin. *Hence, the correct answer is Article 8.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Citizenship under Part II of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Articles 5 to 11** of the Constitution of India govern the provisions related to citizenship.
 
• **Article 5:** Deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution for people domiciled in India.
 
• **Article 6:** Provides citizenship rights for migrants from Pakistan to India.
 
• **Article 7:** Covers the citizenship of persons who migrated to Pakistan but later returned to India.
 
• **Article 9:** States that any person who voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country will lose Indian citizenship.
 
• **Article 10:** Protects the rights of citizenship once acquired and provides for its continuance.
 
• **Article 11:** Grants Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law, enabling future legislation like the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• This Act was enacted by Parliament under **Article 11** to provide detailed provisions for acquiring and terminating citizenship.
 
• It outlines the conditions for citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• **Section 7:** Provides Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) to Indian-origin individuals who were not eligible for full citizenship but wanted a connection with India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora:**
 
 
• India has one of the largest diasporas in the world, with over **32 million people** of Indian origin residing outside India.
 
• Diaspora contributes significantly to India's economy through remittances, which accounted for **$87 billion** in 2021.
 
• The government has launched initiatives like the **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** to engage with the Indian diaspora.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Considerations:**

 
 
• Citizenship provisions are crucial for maintaining India's connection with its diaspora, ensuring their involvement in India’s socio-economic growth.
 
• The government frequently updates policies to strengthen ties with overseas Indians, including issuing **OCI cards** and organizing cultural events.
 
• The Constitution provides a robust framework, and the Citizenship Act complements it with necessary legal provisions.

questions.question: The Indian handicraft industry suffered significant decline under colonial economic policies. What was a major reason for the decline of Indian handicrafts during British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Influx of machine-made British goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Influx of machine-made British goods:** During British rule, India faced a massive influx of **machine-made goods** from Britain. These goods were produced in factories using advanced technology, making them cheaper and more abundant than handcrafted Indian products. This led to the erosion of demand for Indian handicrafts in both domestic and international markets.
 
• The British imposed **high taxes and tariffs** on Indian handmade goods while promoting the sale of British manufactured products. This created an unfair trade environment, further deepening the decline of Indian handicrafts.
 
• Indian artisans, who relied on traditional methods and manual labor, could not compete with the efficiency and lower costs of British machine-made goods. As a result, many artisans lost their livelihoods. *Hence, this was a major reason for the decline of Indian handicrafts.*
 
• **Economic exploitation:** The colonial rulers prioritized the economic interests of Britain over the welfare of Indian industries. They systematically destroyed the thriving handicraft industry by promoting British goods and discouraging Indian production. This caused a significant loss of traditional knowledge and craftsmanship over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of British rule on Indian handicrafts:**

 
 
• Indian handicrafts were widely known for their **intricate designs, quality, and craftsmanship**. Products such as textiles, pottery, and jewelry were exported globally before colonial rule.
 
• The British introduced policies that favored the import of **British goods** and discouraged Indian exports. This led to a decline in the international reputation of Indian handicrafts.
 
 
 
• **Environmental degradation:**
 
 
• While environmental degradation may have had some indirect impact, it was not the primary cause of the decline of Indian handicrafts during British rule. The main reason was the economic exploitation and policy-driven influx of British goods. **Hence, option 1 is not correct.**
 
 
 
• **Rise of Indian industry:**
 
 
• The rise of Indian industry was a later phenomenon, primarily after independence. During British rule, Indian industries were suppressed to promote British goods. **Thus, option 2 is not correct.**
 
 
 
• **Lack of domestic demand:**
 
 
• Indian handicrafts faced reduced domestic demand due to the availability of cheaper British machine-made goods. However, this was a consequence of colonial policies rather than a lack of interest in Indian products. **Hence, option 4 is not fully correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **British Policies:**

 
 
• **Free trade policies:** The British adopted free trade policies that allowed their goods to enter Indian markets without restrictions, while heavily taxing Indian products.
 
• The introduction of **railways and improved transportation** further facilitated the influx of British goods into remote parts of India, saturating the market with cheaper alternatives.
 
 
 
• **Decline of craftsmanship:**
 
 
• The decline of Indian handicrafts led to the loss of traditional skills passed down through generations. Many artisans were forced to take up menial jobs or migrate to urban areas in search of alternative employment.
 
• The decline also resulted in **regional economic disparity**, as areas dependent on handicrafts suffered economic stagnation.

questions.question: Which of the following countries does NOT share a land border with India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India shares **land borders** with several countries, including **Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, and Myanmar.**
 
• The question asks which country **does NOT share a land border** with India. Among the given options, **Sri Lanka** is the correct answer as it does not share a direct land border with India. Instead, it is separated from India by the **Palk Strait**.
 
• **Sri Lanka** is an island nation located in the **Indian Ocean**, just south of India. The **narrow Palk Strait** separates the two countries, making it impossible for Sri Lanka to have a land border with India. Hence, the correct answer is Sri Lanka.
 
• **Afghanistan**, although sharing a very small land border with India in the northwest, is officially recognized as one of the countries bordering India. Hence, Afghanistan is not the correct answer.
 
• **China** shares a significant land border with India in the north. This border includes regions such as **Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, and Sikkim**. Hence, China is not the correct answer.
 
• **Myanmar** shares a land border with India in the northeastern region, particularly in states such as **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Manipur**. Hence, Myanmar is not the correct answer.
 
• ***Thus, the correct answer is Sri Lanka.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's Neighboring Countries:**

 
 
• India shares its borders with **seven countries:** **Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan**.
 
• **Pakistan:** Shares a western border with India. The Radcliffe Line divides the two countries, established during the partition in **1947**.
 
• **China:** Shares a northern border with India, including the disputed regions of **Aksai Chin** and **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• **Bangladesh:** Shares the longest land border with India, stretching over **4,096 kilometers**.
 
• **Myanmar:** Located to the east of India, shares a border with Indian states like **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Manipur**.
 
• **Bhutan:** Shares a border in the Himalayan region, particularly with the states of **Sikkim, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, and Assam**.
 
• **Afghanistan:** India shares a small border with Afghanistan in the **northwest**, known as the **Durand Line**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geopolitical Significance:**

 
 
• **India's land borders** are of strategic importance for security, trade, and cultural exchange. The borders with Pakistan and China are particularly sensitive due to historical disputes.
 
• **India's maritime borders:** Although Sri Lanka does not share a land border with India, the maritime boundary is crucial for trade and bilateral relations.
 
 
 
• **Key Historical and Geographical Facts:**
 
 
• **Adam's Bridge:** It is believed that the **Ramayana** epic mentions this land connection between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• **Palk Strait:** The narrow strait separating India and Sri Lanka is about **40 kilometers wide**.
 
• **Sri Lanka:** Known for its rich cultural heritage, the island nation has historically been connected to India through trade, migration, and cultural exchange.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the Indian government's Bhashini project?

options.text: To create a multilingual AI platform for real-time translation among Indian languages
To establish a national database of dialects
To develop a new programming language for Indian developers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To create a multilingual AI platform for real-time translation among Indian languages.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhashini Project Overview:** The **Bhashini project** is a government initiative by the **Indian Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**. It aims to create a **multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI) platform** designed for facilitating **real-time translation and interpretation** across various Indian languages.
 
• This project is aligned with the vision of **Digital India** and aims to eliminate language barriers across the country by leveraging cutting-edge AI and machine learning technologies.
 
• **Purpose:** The primary goal is to ensure that people from all linguistic backgrounds in India can access **digital content and services in their native languages**. This supports the inclusion of individuals from different regions.
 
• **Focus on Indian Languages:** India is a linguistically diverse country with **22 scheduled languages** and hundreds of dialects. The Bhashini project seeks to bridge the gap by creating a **comprehensive multilingual ecosystem** for communication, especially in regional languages.
 
• **Components:** The project includes the development of **language datasets, APIs, and AI solutions** to support translation, transcription, and interpretation services for Indian languages.
 
• **Applications:** The project can be applied to **education, governance, e-commerce, healthcare, and other domains** to ensure that people from different linguistic backgrounds can access necessary services and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Multilingual AI:**

 
 
• **India's linguistic diversity:** With over **1.3 billion people** speaking a variety of languages, a multilingual AI platform is crucial for fostering inclusivity and removing language as a barrier to communication and information access.
 
• **Applications in public services:** The platform can enable access to **government services, education, and healthcare** in local languages, ensuring that citizens from rural and remote areas are not left behind in the digital revolution.
 
• **Economic impact:** By allowing businesses to interact with customers in their native languages, the project can help boost local and regional economies.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives Supporting Bhashini:**
 
 
• **Digital India Programme:** Launched in **2015**, this initiative aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. Bhashini complements this goal by breaking language barriers.
 
• **Indian Language Internet Alliance (ILIA):** An initiative aimed at increasing Indian language content on the internet, providing a digital space for local languages, which aligns with the Bhashini project.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Context:**

 
 
• **UNESCO:** The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has emphasized the importance of language preservation and promotion for cultural diversity.
 
• **AI in language technologies:** Major companies like **Google** and **Microsoft** are also working on AI-powered translation tools, which further emphasizes the importance of multilingual technology.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The Bhashini project has the potential to position India as a global leader in **language technology**, fostering innovation and collaboration in this domain.
 
• It will also play a crucial role in preserving and promoting India’s **rich linguistic heritage** in the digital age.

questions.question: What was India's Human Development Index (HDI) value in the 2025 UNDP report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.685**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** The **HDI** is a composite index used to measure and compare a country's development. It includes three major dimensions: **health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita).**
 
• According to the **2025 UNDP Report, India's HDI value was recorded as 0.685**. This value represents India's progress across the three dimensions: health, education, and living standards.
 
• The HDI value of **0.685** places India in the medium human development category. *Hence, the correct answer is Option 3.*
 
• **India's HDI Growth:** Over the years, India has seen steady progress in improving its HDI value due to initiatives targeting poverty alleviation, healthcare improvements, and educational reforms.
 
• The HDI value is calculated annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).** It serves as a global benchmark to assess a country's development level. *Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• Introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in **1990**, the HDI provides a summary measure of human development.
 
• The HDI focuses on three dimensions: **health, education, and living standards.** It helps in assessing the social and economic development of a country.
 
 
 
• **Key Components of HDI:**
 
 
• **Health:** Measured by the **life expectancy at birth**, which indicates the average lifespan of individuals in a country.
 
• **Education:** Measured using the **mean years of schooling** for adults and the **expected years of schooling** for children.
 
• **Standard of Living:** Measured using the **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, adjusted for purchasing power parity.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Progress:**
 
 
• India has shown consistent improvement in its HDI ranking over the years, reflecting efforts to enhance healthcare, education, and economic conditions.
 
• Initiatives such as **Ayushman Bharat**, **Skill India Mission**, and **Digital India** have contributed to better living standards and opportunities for growth.
 
• In the **2025 UNDP report, India's HDI value of 0.685** places it among countries with medium human development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global HDI Rankings:**

 
 
• Countries are categorized into **low, medium, high, and very high human development** based on their HDI values.
 
• The **highest HDI rankings** are typically occupied by developed nations, such as **Norway**, **Switzerland**, and **Ireland**.
 
 
 
• **India's Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite improvements, India faces challenges like **poverty, inequality, and healthcare infrastructure.**
 
• Government schemes such as **National Health Mission** and **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan** aim to address these issues.
 
• Improving HDI is crucial for sustainable development and achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

questions.question: Which desktop element in Windows displays system notifications, date and time, and background apps status?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Notification Area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Notification Area**, also referred to as the system tray, is a key desktop element in **Windows**. It is located at the bottom-right corner of the **desktop screen**, near the taskbar.
 
• This area displays important **system notifications**, such as updates, security alerts, and application messages, ensuring users are informed about the system's status.
 
• It shows the **date and time**, which is an essential feature allowing users to keep track of their schedule directly from the desktop.
 
• The **Notification Area** also provides information about the status of **background applications** running on the system, such as antivirus programs, network connections, or battery status (on laptops).
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Notification Area**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **File Explorer:**

 
 
• **File Explorer** is a tool used for navigating and managing files and folders on a **Windows system**.
 
• It does not display system notifications or the status of background applications.
 
• **Example:** Users can open, move, copy, or delete files using File Explorer.
 
 
 
• **Start Menu:**
 
 
• The **Start Menu** is the central hub for accessing programs, settings, and features of a **Windows system**.
 
• It is located on the bottom-left corner of the desktop and does not display system notifications or time.
 
• **Example:** The Start Menu is used to open applications or search for files on the computer.
 
 
 
• **Control Panel:**
 
 
• **Control Panel** is a Windows feature used for changing system settings and configurations.
 
• It allows users to modify settings such as **network preferences, hardware configurations**, and user accounts, but does not display system notifications.
 
• **Example:** Changing the display resolution or adding a printer is done via the Control Panel.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Features of the Notification Area:**

 
 
• The Notification Area includes icons for system processes such as **volume control, network status, battery level, and antivirus software.**
 
• Users can customize which icons appear in the Notification Area via **Taskbar Settings**.
 
• It often provides quick access to specific settings by right-clicking on the icons.
 
 
 
• **How Notifications Work:**
 
 
• Notifications appear as pop-ups on the lower-right side of the screen, displaying important updates or alerts.
 
• Users can interact with these notifications by clicking on them, which often redirects to the respective application or setting.

questions.question: Article 323B of the Constitution of India (added by the 42nd Amendment) empowers the Parliament to establish tribunals for adjudication of matters related to certain subjects. Which of the following matters is specifically covered under Article 323B?

options.text: Matters such as taxation, foreign exchange, land reforms, etc., which can be assigned to tribunals by legislation
Recruitment and service conditions of public servants (civil services)
Only industrial disputes between employers and workers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Matters such as taxation, foreign exchange, land reforms, etc., which can be assigned to tribunals by legislation.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 323B** of the **Indian Constitution**, introduced by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, empowers **Parliament** and state legislatures to establish tribunals for specific matters.
 
• The matters covered under Article 323B include **taxation, foreign exchange, land reforms, ceiling on urban property, elections, and industrial and labour disputes.**
 
• Tribunals established under Article 323B are intended to provide speedy and specialized justice in these domains. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• **Option 2** mentions the appointment of Supreme Court judges, which is not covered under Article 323B. It is governed by **Articles 124 and 217** of the Indian Constitution, making this option *incorrect.*
 
• **Option 3** mentions recruitment and service conditions of public servants. This is a subject matter for tribunals under **Article 323A**, not Article 323B. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Option 4** suggests that Article 323B covers only industrial disputes between employers and workers. However, Article 323B encompasses more subjects beyond just industrial disputes. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 323B:**

 
 
• Article 323B was introduced through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976**, which aimed to strengthen the tribunal system in India for adjudication of specific matters.
 
• Matters covered under Article 323B include **taxation, foreign exchange, industrial disputes, elections, land reforms, urban property ceilings, production, procurement, and distribution of foodstuffs, among others.**
 
• The tribunals established under Article 323B are independent judicial bodies designed to provide speedy justice in specialized areas, reducing the burden on regular courts.
 
 
 
• **Difference between Article 323A and Article 323B:**
 
 
• **Article 323A** deals exclusively with tribunals for **service matters** related to recruitment and conditions of service of public servants.
 
• **Article 323B** covers a broader range of subjects, including taxation, industrial disputes, elections, and land reforms, among others.
 
• Unlike Article 323A, which allows only the Parliament to establish tribunals, Article 323B empowers both **Parliament and state legislatures** to create tribunals for matters listed therein.
 
 
 
• **Tribunals in India:**
 
 
• Tribunals play a key role in ensuring speedy and efficient justice in specific areas such as administrative disputes, taxation issues, and industrial matters.
 
• Examples of tribunals set up under Article 323B include the **Income Tax Appellate Tribunal** (for taxation matters) and the **Central Administrative Tribunal** (under Article 323A).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Provisions of Article 323B:**

 
 
• Tribunals under Article 323B are expected to function independently, ensuring fair and expedient resolution of disputes in specialized areas.
 
• These tribunals have the power to adjudicate disputes, hear appeals, and enforce laws related to the matters listed in the article.
 
• The establishment of these tribunals is part of efforts to address the problem of judicial backlog and provide focused expertise in resolving disputes.

questions.question: Which sector(s) employed the largest share of the working population in India on the eve of independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the eve of India’s independence in **1947**, the **primary sector** was the largest employer of the Indian workforce. This sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and other allied activities.
 
• The Indian economy was largely **agrarian** during British rule, with over 70% of the population dependent on agriculture for their livelihood.
 
• The economy was predominantly rural, with limited industrialization and negligible development in the **secondary** (manufacturing) and **tertiary** (services) sectors.
 
• The **primary sector** accounted for a substantial share of the national income, but it was characterized by low productivity, outdated technology, and a lack of investment.
 
• The exploitation of Indian agriculture under British colonial policies, such as the **zamindari system** and high land revenue demands, further contributed to the dominance of the primary sector in terms of employment, as most of the population relied on subsistence farming.
 
• The **secondary sector** (industrial sector) was underdeveloped during colonial rule as the British policies discouraged the growth of Indian industries to ensure dependence on British manufactured goods.
 
• The **tertiary sector**, which includes services like trade, transport, and banking, was also underdeveloped and catered primarily to the needs of colonial administration and foreign trade.
 
• Thus, the majority of the Indian population at the time of independence was employed in the **primary sector**, and the economy was heavily dependent on agriculture. *Hence, the correct answer is Primary sector.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• The primary sector involves activities that are directly dependent on natural resources, such as **agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining**.
 
• In India, before independence, a significant majority of the population was engaged in agriculture and allied activities as their primary source of livelihood.
 
• The primary sector contributed the most to India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) during colonial rule, but it was marked by a lack of modernization and low productivity.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• The secondary sector includes industries that produce finished goods from raw materials, such as **manufacturing, construction, and industrial production**.
 
• During British rule, the secondary sector was underdeveloped as the colonial powers prioritized raw material extraction from India for industries in Britain, while deliberately restricting the growth of Indian industries.
 
• Examples include the decline of the Indian textile industry due to competition from British imports and the lack of capital investment in industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• The tertiary sector includes services like **trade, transport, banking, communication, and administration**.
 
• During colonial rule, the tertiary sector primarily served the needs of the British administration and foreign trade, with limited contribution to the general population’s employment.
 
• It was small in size compared to the primary sector and did not play a significant role in providing employment.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Developments:**
 
 
• After independence, efforts were made to diversify the economy by promoting industrialization and developing the secondary and tertiary sectors.
 
• Policies like the **Five-Year Plans**, establishment of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), and Green Revolution significantly contributed to reducing the over-reliance on agriculture.
 
• In recent years, the tertiary sector has emerged as the largest contributor to GDP, while the share of the primary sector has declined.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Agrarian Economy:** India’s economy during colonial rule was predominantly agrarian, with a majority of the population engaged in agriculture and related activities.
 
• **Exploitation of Indian Agriculture:** The British implemented exploitative systems like the **zamindari system**, which led to widespread poverty and low agricultural productivity.
 
• **Limited Industrialization:** The British policies hindered the development of industries in India, restricting employment opportunities in the secondary sector.
 
• **Economic Transition:** Post-independence, India witnessed a shift from an agrarian economy to a more diversified one, with significant growth in industrial and service sectors.
 
• **Current Scenario:** As of recent times, the **tertiary sector** has become the largest contributor to India’s GDP, while the primary sector employs a lower percentage of the population compared to the past.

questions.question: Impulse is defined as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**product of force and time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Impulse** is defined as the **product of force and the time interval** over which the force acts. Mathematically, Impulse (J) = Force (F) × Time (t).
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity, as both force and time are involved. It has the same direction as the applied force.
 
• The **SI unit** of impulse is the **Newton-second (Ns)**, which is equivalent to the unit of momentum.
 
• Impulse is closely related to the concept of **momentum**. According to the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse is equal to the change in momentum of an object: J = Δp = m × Δv.
 
• Impulse is significant in analyzing collisions and impacts. For example, when a baseball bat hits a ball, the force exerted during the short time of contact changes the ball's momentum, which is described by impulse.
 
• The other options (rate of change of force, change in displacement, product of mass and velocity) are incorrect because they do not represent impulse. **Rate of change of force** is related to jerk, **change in displacement** is connected to distance, and **product of mass and velocity** is momentum, not impulse.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is product of force and time.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impulse and Momentum Theorem:**

 
 
• The impulse-momentum theorem states that the impulse experienced by an object is equal to the change in its momentum.
 
• Mathematically, J = Δp = m × Δv, where J is impulse, Δp is the change in momentum, m is mass, and Δv is the change in velocity.
 
• This relationship is derived from Newton’s second law (F = m × a), considering the time interval of the applied force.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Impulse:**
 
 
• Impulse is crucial in sports, such as cricket, baseball, and football, where players exert force for a short time to change the momentum of balls.
 
• It is used in designing safety equipment like airbags and helmets to reduce the effect of sudden impacts by increasing the time of collision.
 
• Impulse is also used in rocket propulsion, where gases are expelled over a short time to generate thrust.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• A soccer player kicking a ball applies a force for a short duration, generating an impulse that changes the ball's speed and direction.
 
• In car crashes, the sudden application of force can cause significant damage. Airbags reduce the impact force by increasing the time of collision, thereby reducing the impulse on the passengers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impulse Calculation:**

 
 
• Impulse can be calculated using the formula J = F × t, where **F** is the force applied and **t** is the time duration of the force.
 
• If the force is not constant, impulse is calculated as the integral of force over the time interval: J = ∫F dt.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Examples:**
 
 
• During a boxing match, the punch delivered by a boxer generates impulse that affects the opponent's momentum.
 
• When a tennis player hits the ball with a racket, the force exerted over a brief time changes the ball's velocity and direction.

questions.question: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526, replacing the Lodi Dynasty with Mughal rule in India. It was fought between Ibrahim Lodi and _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The First Battle of Panipat** took place on **April 21, 1526**. It marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• The battle was fought between **Babar**, the founder of the Mughal Empire, and **Ibrahim Lodi**, the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty. *This statement is correct.*
 
• Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodi, ending the rule of the **Lodi dynasty** and establishing the Mughal dynasty in India.
 
• The battle was significant as it introduced **modern warfare techniques** to India, including the use of gunpowder, artillery, and field tactics.
 
• Babar's forces were smaller in number compared to Ibrahim Lodi's army, but their superior strategy and advanced weaponry played a crucial role in their victory.
 
• The victory in this battle enabled Babar to lay the foundation of the **Mughal Empire** in India. *Hence, the correct answer is Babar.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The First Battle of Panipat:**

 
 
• The battle was fought near **Panipat**, a town in present-day Haryana, India.
 
• Babar's army consisted of approximately **12,000 troops**, while Ibrahim Lodi's force was significantly larger, numbering around **100,000 soldiers** (including camp followers).
 
• Babar used innovative warfare techniques, such as the deployment of **field artillery** and the **Tulughma (encircling tactics)**, which were not known to Indian armies at that time.
 
 
 
• **Babar's Role and Legacy:**
 
 
• Babar was a descendant of **Timur** on his father's side and **Genghis Khan** on his mother's side.
 
• He was invited by **Daulat Khan Lodi**, a regional governor under Ibrahim Lodi, to invade India and overthrow the Lodi ruler.
 
• After the victory in the First Battle of Panipat, Babar established the **Mughal Empire**, which ruled India for over three centuries.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi:**
 
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the **Lodi dynasty**, which was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He was known for his autocratic rule and alienated many of his nobles, which ultimately led to his downfall.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Battle:**
 
 
• The battle was a turning point in Indian history as it marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the **Mughal Empire**.
 
• Babar's victory demonstrated the importance of modern military technology and tactics in warfare.
 
• The battle also showcased the weakness of Indian armies in adapting to new military strategies and equipment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Use of Gunpowder:**

 
 
• The First Battle of Panipat is considered one of the earliest battles in India to involve the use of **gunpowder firearms** and field artillery.
 
• Babar's artillery, commanded by **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**, played a decisive role in the victory.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Lodi dynasty was already weakened by internal conflicts and discontent among its nobles.
 
• The battle was part of a larger struggle for power in North India during the early 16th century.
 
 
 
• **Consequences:**
 
 
• Babar's victory led to the establishment of the **Mughal Empire**, which became one of the most powerful empires in Indian history.
 
• The battle marked a shift in military tactics and weaponry in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which leader played the most crucial role in integrating princely states into India postindependence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, often referred to as the **Iron Man of India**, played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union after independence.
 
• At the time of India's independence in **1947**, there were **562 princely states**. These states were semi-independent entities, and their rulers were given the choice to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent. This created a complex challenge for the newly formed Indian government.
 
• Sardar Patel, as the first **Deputy Prime Minister** and **Minister of Home Affairs** of independent India, took charge of integrating these states into the Indian Union.
 
• He used a combination of diplomacy, negotiation, and strategic pressure to convince the rulers of princely states to accede to India. Patel was assisted by **V.P. Menon**, who played an instrumental role in drafting the agreements and facilitating the process.
 
• Patel persuaded the rulers to sign the **Instrument of Accession**, ensuring their states would become part of India while retaining autonomy in certain internal matters.
 
• His efforts led to the peaceful accession of most princely states, including large ones like **Hyderabad, Junagarh, and Kashmir**, which posed unique challenges.
 
• In cases where peaceful negotiations failed, Patel used military action, as seen in the **police action in Hyderabad** (Operation Polo) to integrate the state into India.
 
• Through his firm resolve and visionary leadership, Patel ensured the territorial integrity of the newly independent India, setting the foundation for a unified nation.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:**

 
 
• Known as the **architect of Indian integration**, Patel was responsible for bringing together the diverse princely states into the Indian Union in a short span of time.
 
• He used his skills in **diplomacy** and pragmatic decision-making to address complex political situations and avoid fragmentation of the country.
 
 
 
• **Challenges faced during integration:**
 
 
• Several princely states, including **Hyderabad, Junagarh, and Kashmir**, initially resisted accession to India. Patel's strategic approach ensured their peaceful or forceful integration.
 
• The use of military action, such as **Operation Polo** in Hyderabad, demonstrated Patel's resolve to preserve India's unity.
 
 
 
• **Instrument of Accession:**
 
 
• The **Instrument of Accession** was a legal document signed by the rulers of princely states agreeing to join India. This ensured that the sovereignty of India was upheld while granting some autonomy to the states.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Sardar Patel:**
 
 
• Patel’s efforts ensured the creation of a politically stable and unified Indian state, which has been crucial for the country’s development.
 
• To honor his contributions, the **Statue of Unity**, the world’s tallest statue, was built in Gujarat in **2018**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **BR Ambedkar:**

 
 
• Known as the **architect of the Indian Constitution**, Ambedkar worked primarily on establishing a framework for governance and social justice in India.
 
• He did not play a direct role in the integration of princely states.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• As the first **Prime Minister** of India, Nehru focused on building the political and economic framework of the nation.
 
• Although he supported Patel in the integration process, Nehru’s role was more prominent in post-independence governance.
 
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose:**
 
 
• Bose was a prominent leader in the **Indian freedom struggle**. He formed the **Indian National Army** to fight against British colonial rule.
 
• While his contributions to independence were immense, he did not play a direct role in post-independence state integration.

questions.question: Which Act first created the position of a Governor-General of India with civil and military authority?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act 1833**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** was a significant legislative act passed by the British Parliament to reform the administration of British India.
 
• It marked the end of the trading functions of the **East India Company** and transformed it into an administrative body.
 
• The Act created the position of **Governor-General of India**, granting him both **civil and military authority**. This was a pivotal change, as it centralized power in India. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• The first Governor-General of India under this Act was **Lord William Bentinck**.
 
• The Act also allowed the Governor-General to pass laws for the entire country, thus marking a step toward legal and administrative centralization.
 
• It introduced the concept of an **Indian Law Commission** to codify laws in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**

 
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** was enacted to address administrative inefficiencies and provide centralized control over British India.
 
• It abolished the trading rights of the **East India Company**, making it purely an administrative and political entity.
 
• The creation of the **Governor-General of India** was an essential step in establishing British authority across the country.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Governor-General of India:**
 
 
• The Governor-General had the authority to legislate for all territories under British control in India.
 
• The position centralized administrative power and introduced uniformity in governance.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Acts:**
 
 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:** It was the first attempt to regulate the affairs of the East India Company. However, it did not create the position of Governor-General of India but introduced the Governor-General of Bengal.
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:** This Act strengthened British control over the East India Company's administration but did not create the Governor-General of India.
 
• **Government of India Act 1858:** This Act marked the transfer of control of India from the East India Company to the British Crown, further centralizing power but occurring after the Charter Act of 1833.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of the Charter Act of 1833:**

 
 
• The Act marked a significant shift in the governance model of British India, centralizing power under the Governor-General of India.
 
• It also introduced measures to ensure the codification of laws and laid the foundation for modern legal systems in India.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Other Acts:**
 
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** and **Pitt’s India Act of 1784** were significant in establishing British control but did not centralize authority under a single Governor-General of India.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1858** followed the Charter Act of 1833 and took steps to transfer power from the East India Company to the British Crown.

__
 
• **Article 6** of the **Indian Constitution** addresses the citizenship of persons who migrated to India from **Pakistan**.
 
• This provision specifically applies to individuals who were born in undivided India and moved to India after the partition in **1947**.
 
• It grants **Indian citizenship** to those who migrated from Pakistan before **July 19, 1948**, provided they or either of their parents were born in undivided India and had been residing in India since migration.
 
• For those who migrated after **July 19, 1948**, Indian citizenship is granted if they registered themselves as citizens of India under the prescribed procedure.
 
• The provision also specifies that the registration process must be conducted by an officer appointed by the Government of India.
 
• This article is part of the broader framework of the Constitution that defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• It aims to address the displacement and migration caused by the partition of India, ensuring legal recognition of citizenship for affected individuals.

• The partition of India in **1947** led to large-scale migration between India and Pakistan due to religious and communal reasons.
 
• Millions of people moved across borders, creating a significant need for a legal framework to grant citizenship to migrants.
 
 
 
• **Provisions under Article 6:**
 
 
• Migrants who entered India before **July 19, 1948**, and lived in India since migration automatically qualified for citizenship.
 
• Those who migrated after this date were required to register themselves with the appropriate authority to obtain Indian citizenship.
 
• The registration process required proof of residence in India and verification by the appointed officer.
 
 
 
• **Key Legislative Acts:**

• It ensures that people who migrated from Pakistan due to religious or political persecution are given the right to Indian citizenship.

• The partition led to the displacement of millions of people, necessitating legal measures to address their citizenship status.
 
• Article 6 played a crucial role in integrating migrants into the socio-political framework of India.

• The SDGs are also referred to as the **Global Goals**. They are a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that all people enjoy peace and prosperity by the year **2030**.

• **Goal 8:** Decent Work and Economic Growth – Promotes sustained, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all.
 
• **Goal 9:** Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure – Builds resilient infrastructure, promotes inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fosters innovation.
 
• **Goal 10:** Reduced Inequalities – Reduces inequality within and among countries.

• **Goal 12:** Responsible Consumption and Production – Ensures sustainable consumption and production patterns.

• **Goal 14:** Life Below Water – Conserves and sustainably uses the oceans, seas, and marine resources.

• **Importance of SDGs:**

• According to the **Ministry of Agriculture data** from **1950–51 to 2014–15**, the land use category of **barren and wasteland** has shown a **declining trend**.
 
• This decline is primarily due to the efforts towards converting barren and wasteland into usable land for agriculture, afforestation, and other developmental purposes. *Hence, the correct option is barren and wasteland.*
 
• The other options like net sown area, forest area, and area under non-agricultural use have not shown the same consistent declining trend when analyzed over the same period. For example, forest areas have increased due to afforestation efforts, and non-agricultural land use has expanded with urbanization and industrialization. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

• **Area under Non-Agricultural Use:**

• Under the **National Afforestation Programme (NAP)**, efforts are made to enhance forest and tree cover to combat climate change, conserve biodiversity, and restore degraded lands.
