questions.question: In which year did Andre-Marie Ampère publish his magnum opus ‘Mathematical Theory of Electrodynamic Phenomena Deduced Solely from Experiments’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1827**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andre-Marie Ampère**, a French physicist and mathematician, is best known for his groundbreaking work in the field of **electrodynamics**, which laid the foundation for modern electromagnetism.
 
• In **1827**, Ampère published his magnum opus titled **“Mathematical Theory of Electrodynamic Phenomena Deduced Solely from Experiments”**, which is considered one of the most significant contributions to the study of electricity and magnetism.
 
• This work provided a complete theoretical framework for understanding the interaction of electric currents and magnetic fields, marking the beginning of the field of electrodynamics. *Hence, the correct year is 1827.*
 
• Andre-Marie Ampère's name is immortalized in the **unit of electric current**, the **Ampere**, which is a testament to his lasting impact on physics.
 
• The other options like **1833**, **1818**, and **1811** are incorrect because they do not correspond to the publication year of this significant work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Andre-Marie Ampère:**

 
 
• **Andre-Marie Ampère** (1775–1836) was a pioneer in the study of electromagnetism and is often considered the **father of electrodynamics**.
 
• He formulated the **Ampère's law**, which mathematically describes the magnetic force between two electric currents.
 
 
 
• **About the Magnum Opus:**
 
 
• Ampère's book **“Mathematical Theory of Electrodynamic Phenomena”** was a pioneering work that included experimental results and theoretical analysis of electric currents and magnetic fields.
 
• This publication firmly established the field of **electrodynamics** and introduced key concepts that influenced later scientists like James Clerk Maxwell.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Science:**
 
 
• **Ampère's work** demonstrated that two wires carrying electric currents exert a force on each other, which could be attractive or repulsive depending on the direction of the currents.
 
• He introduced the concept of the **electrodynamic molecule**, which was an early attempt to describe magnetic phenomena at the molecular level.
 
 
 
• **About the Ampere (Unit):**
 
 
• The SI unit of electric current, the **Ampere**, is named after Andre-Marie Ampère in recognition of his contributions to the field of electromagnetism.
 
• One Ampere is defined as the constant current that, when maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length and negligible cross-section placed one meter apart in a vacuum, would produce a force of **2 × 10⁻⁷ newtons per meter** of length between the conductors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electrodynamics:**

 
 
• Electrodynamics is the branch of physics that studies the interaction between **electric currents** and **magnetic fields**. It forms the basis of many modern technologies, including electric motors and generators.
 
• Ampère's contributions to electrodynamics influenced the work of later scientists, including **Michael Faraday** and **James Clerk Maxwell**, who further developed the understanding of electromagnetism.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The publication of Ampère's work in **1827** marked a turning point in the study of physics, leading to a deeper understanding of electromagnetic forces and their applications in technology.
 
• His discoveries paved the way for the development of electrical engineering and technologies such as **telecommunications**, **power generation**, and **electronic devices**.

questions.question: Harold C Urey was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, in 1934:

options.text: for discovery in the chemistry of the transuranium elements
for the discovery of heavy hydrogen
for the discovery and development of conductive polymers
for the development of the density-functional theory

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**for the discovery of heavy hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harold C. Urey** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1934**.
 
• The award was given for his **discovery of heavy hydrogen**, also known as **deuterium**.
 
• Heavy hydrogen (**deuterium**) is an isotope of hydrogen with one neutron in addition to the single proton in the nucleus of the atom, making it heavier than regular hydrogen. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The discovery of deuterium was a breakthrough in the field of **isotopes**, contributing significantly to the understanding of atomic structures and nuclear chemistry.
 
• Urey’s discovery laid the foundation for advancements in **nuclear reactions** and studies of the behavior of isotopes in chemical processes. *Hence, the discovery is of paramount importance.*
 
• The discovery also had practical applications, such as in **nuclear power**, **thermonuclear reactions**, and as a tracer in **biological and chemical research.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Harold C. Urey:**

 
 
• **Harold Clayton Urey** (1893–1981) was an American physical chemist and a pioneer in the study of isotopes.
 
• He discovered **deuterium** in **1931** and subsequently received the **Nobel Prize** for this significant achievement.
 
• Urey’s work also contributed to the development of the **Manhattan Project**, which focused on nuclear weapon development during World War II.
 
 
 
• **About Heavy Hydrogen (Deuterium):**
 
 
• **Deuterium** is a naturally occurring isotope of hydrogen, with a nucleus composed of one proton and one neutron.
 
• It is found in small amounts in **water molecules**, which are referred to as **heavy water** when enriched with deuterium.
 
• **Applications:** Used in **nuclear reactors**, **biological research**, and **spectroscopic studies**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nobel Prize in Chemistry:**
 
 
• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognizes **groundbreaking discoveries** that contribute to the advancement of science and practical applications globally.
 
• Urey’s recognition highlighted the importance of **isotope chemistry** in modern scientific progress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Isotopes:**

 
 
• **Isotopes** are variants of elements with the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to the presence of varying numbers of neutrons.
 
• **Deuterium** is a stable isotope of hydrogen and does not undergo radioactive decay.
 
 
 
• **Heavy Water (D₂O):**
 
 
• Heavy water is water in which the hydrogen atoms have been replaced with **deuterium atoms**.
 
• **Uses:** Heavy water is a crucial moderator in **nuclear reactors** and is used in **neutron scattering experiments.**

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is primarily used by the RBI for monetary policy implementation in the post 1991 reform era?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Repo Rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate** is the primary instrument used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** for monetary policy implementation, especially in the post-1991 reform era.
 
• The **Repo Rate** refers to the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks in the short term, usually against government securities.
 
• By increasing or decreasing the **Repo Rate**, the RBI influences the liquidity in the banking system and controls inflation or stimulates economic growth. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The tools mentioned in the other options, such as **Export Incentives**, **Tariff Rates**, and **Direct Taxes**, are primarily fiscal policy measures, not monetary policy instruments. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• In the post-1991 economic reforms, the RBI shifted its focus to indirect tools like the **Repo Rate** to efficiently manage monetary policy. The use of direct instruments, such as Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), has decreased in importance. *Hence, the correct answer is Repo Rate.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate:**

 
 
• **Repo Rate** is an important tool of monetary policy used by central banks globally, including the RBI, to regulate liquidity and inflation.
 
• In India, the **RBI** adjusts the **Repo Rate** depending on the economic situation. For instance, the rate is lowered during recessions to encourage borrowing and spending, while it is increased during inflationary periods to curb excessive liquidity.
 
• During the pandemic, the RBI lowered the **Repo Rate** to support economic activity and provide relief to borrowers.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy vs Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy** involves government spending and taxation measures, such as **Direct Taxes** and **Export Incentives**, to influence economic conditions.
 
• **Monetary Policy**, managed by the RBI, includes tools like **Repo Rate**, **Reverse Repo Rate**, and **Open Market Operations** to control inflation, ensure price stability, and regulate the money supply.
 
 
 
• **Direct Taxes and Tariff Rates:**
 
 
• **Direct Taxes** are levied directly on income or profits, such as Income Tax and Corporate Tax. These are fiscal measures and not used for monetary policy implementation.
 
• **Tariff Rates** are used to influence international trade and are part of fiscal policy rather than monetary policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Repo Rate in India:**

 
 
• The **Repo Rate** is determined by the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which was constituted under the **RBI Act of 1934**.
 
• The MPC meets bi-monthly to assess economic conditions and decide on the **Repo Rate** adjustments.
 
• **Current Repo Rate (as of October 2023):** 6.5% (subject to change depending on inflation and economic trends).
 
 
 
• **Impacts of Repo Rate Changes:**
 
 
• An increase in the **Repo Rate** leads to higher borrowing costs for commercial banks, reducing liquidity in the economy.
 
• A decrease in the **Repo Rate** encourages borrowing, boosts liquidity, and stimulates economic growth.

questions.question: Which economic system dominated India on the eve of independence (in 1947)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colonial agrarian economy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's economy during the time of independence in **1947** was primarily an agrarian economy. This means that agriculture was the dominant sector, employing around **85% of the population**.
 
• The British colonial rulers had established an exploitative economic system that focused on **extracting resources** from India and exporting raw materials to Britain.
 
• The British introduced the **zamindari system** (land revenue system), which led to the exploitation of farmers. Farmers were heavily taxed, and many were left in poverty.
 
• The colonial economy was structured in a way that hindered industrial development in India. Instead, it promoted the imports of British manufactured goods, creating an imbalance in trade.
 
• The economy lacked significant industrialization, with limited development in sectors like textiles, steel, and other manufacturing industries. As a result, India depended heavily on agriculture.
 
• The infrastructure, such as railways and communication systems, introduced by the British was largely meant to serve their own administrative and economic interests, such as the transportation of raw materials.
 
• By the time of independence, India had a **low per capita income**, high levels of poverty, and widespread unemployment, which were the result of prolonged colonial exploitation. *Hence, the correct answer is "Colonial agrarian economy."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Colonial Agrarian Economy:**

 
 
• The economy was predominantly rural, with the majority of people engaged in **subsistence agriculture.**
 
• India became a supplier of raw materials like **cotton, jute, and spices** to British industries and a market for their finished goods.
 
• There was a lack of modern agricultural technology, leading to **low productivity** and frequent famines.
 
• The **zamindari system** and other land revenue systems caused widespread exploitation of farmers by landlords and moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Colonial Rule on India’s Economy:**
 
 
• The Indian economy faced **deindustrialization**, particularly in the traditional handicrafts and textile industries.
 
• The **drain of wealth** theory, as explained by **Dadabhai Naoroji**, highlighted how resources were extracted from India to enrich Britain.
 
• The lack of capital investment in industries and infrastructure for the benefit of Indians left the country economically backward.
 
 
 
• **Contrasting Economic Systems:**
 
 
• **Import substitution industrialization:** Adopted later in India post-independence to reduce dependency on imports and promote domestic industries.
 
• **Global free market:** India did not adopt this system at the time of independence, as the focus was on self-reliance and economic recovery.
 
• **Socialist planned economy:** This system was introduced in India after independence with the adoption of the **Five-Year Plans** starting in 1951.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The British policies resulted in **stagnant economic growth**, with the agricultural sector unable to sustain the growing population.
 
• The **per capita income** during the colonial period barely increased, and the standard of living of the average Indian deteriorated.
 
• The colonial economy left India with a legacy of poverty, high illiteracy rates, and underdeveloped industries, which the country had to address post-independence.

questions.question: Which of the following is a discretionary power of the President of India?

options.text: Dissolving the Lok Sabha without advice
Appointing the Chief Justice of India
Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority
Giving assent to a Money Bill

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Discretionary powers of the President of India:** The President of India holds discretionary powers, which are exercised only under certain circumstances. These powers allow the President to act without the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• When no political party secures a clear majority in the Lok Sabha, the President has the authority to use his/her discretion in appointing the Prime Minister. *Hence, appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority is a discretionary power.*
 
• The President may invite the leader of the largest party or coalition to form the government, provided they can prove majority support in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Other situations where the President exercises discretionary powers include dismissing a government when it loses majority and recommending the dissolution of Lok Sabha if no viable government can be formed.
 
• The President does not have the discretion to dissolve the Lok Sabha without the advice of the Council of Ministers. This is governed by Article 85 of the Constitution. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Appointing the Chief Justice of India is not a discretionary power. The President appoints the Chief Justice based on established conventions and recommendations from the judiciary. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Giving assent to a Money Bill is not a discretionary power of the President. Under Article 110, the President can only approve or reject a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the President:**

 
 
• Discretionary powers are exercised by the President in situations where the advice of the Council of Ministers is not available or applicable.
 
• Examples include appointing the Prime Minister when no party secures a majority in the Lok Sabha or dissolving the Lok Sabha when no viable government can be formed.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Prime Minister:**
 
 
• When no single party achieves a majority, the President invites the leader of the largest coalition or party to form the government.
 
• The appointed Prime Minister must prove majority support in the Lok Sabha within a stipulated time frame.
 
• **Example:** In 1989, when no party achieved a majority, then President **R. Venkataraman** appointed **V. P. Singh** as Prime Minister after consultation with various leaders.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• **Article 75:** It states that the President appoints the Prime Minister and other members of the Council of Ministers.
 
• **Article 85:** The President summons, prorogues, and dissolves the Lok Sabha based on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President’s discretionary powers are used in exceptional circumstances, ensuring the democratic process is upheld.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Discretionary Powers:**

 
 
• The discretionary powers of the President are limited and are exercised only in rare situations like a hung parliament or no clear majority.
 
• These powers are intended to maintain the smooth functioning of parliamentary democracy and ensure governance continuity.
 
 
 
• **Historical Examples:**
 
 
• **1996:** After the general elections, then-President **Shankar Dayal Sharma** appointed **A. B. Vajpayee** as Prime Minister for 13 days when BJP emerged as the single largest party but failed to prove majority.
 
• **1989:** When Congress lost the majority, President **R. Venkataraman** appointed **V. P. Singh** as Prime Minister, who later proved his majority in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The Gulf of Mannar lies between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Gulf of Mannar** is a shallow bay area located in the Indian Ocean. It lies between the southeastern coast of **India** and the northwestern coast of **Sri Lanka**.
 
• It is part of the larger Laccadive Sea and is a well-known marine biodiversity hotspot, with rich coral reefs, seagrass beds, and marine ecosystems.
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is separated from the Palk Strait by the **Rameswaram Island** and the **Adam’s Bridge** (also known as Ram Setu), a chain of limestone shoals connecting India and Sri Lanka. *This confirms that the Gulf of Mannar lies between India and Sri Lanka.*
 
• The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, established in **1989**, covers an area of around **10,500 square kilometers**. It is India’s first marine biosphere reserve, protecting the rich biodiversity of this region.
 
• The area is known for its high ecological importance, being home to over **3,600 species** of marine flora and fauna, including endangered species like the **Dugong (sea cow)**.
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is also historically significant due to its role in ancient trade routes connecting Southeast Asia with South India and Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography of the Gulf of Mannar:**

 
 
• The Gulf of Mannar extends from **Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu**, India to **Mannar Island**, Sri Lanka. It is approximately **160 kilometers** wide.
 
• It is bordered by the **Coromandel Coast** in India and the **Sri Lankan coastal plains**. The waters are relatively shallow, making it ideal for coral growth and marine life.
 
 
 
• **Marine Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is renowned for its rich marine biodiversity, including **coral reefs**, **pearl banks**, **seagrass ecosystems**, and **marine algae**.
 
• It supports endangered species like the **Dugong**, **green sea turtles**, and **whale sharks**.
 
• The region is also a major contributor to India’s **marine fisheries** industry, providing livelihoods to thousands of coastal communities.
 
 
 
• **Adam’s Bridge (Ram Setu):**
 
 
• Adam’s Bridge consists of a series of limestone shoals and sandbanks that historically connected India and Sri Lanka. It is believed to be submerged due to rising sea levels over time.
 
• According to Hindu mythology, this bridge was constructed by Lord Rama’s army to rescue Goddess Sita from Ravana in Lanka.
 
• Modern geological studies suggest that it is a naturally formed structure, though it holds cultural and religious significance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Trade Significance:**

 
 
• The Gulf of Mannar was historically a major trade route for spices, pearls, and other goods between **Southeast Asia** and the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• Ancient Tamil literature mentions the Gulf of Mannar as a center for **pearl diving**. The region’s pearl banks were famous for producing high-quality pearls.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Concerns:**
 
 
• The Gulf of Mannar faces threats from **pollution**, **overfishing**, and **coral bleaching** due to climate change.
 
• Conservation efforts like the establishment of the **Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park** aim to protect its unique biodiversity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Melt and Pour' rule introduced in the DMI&SP Policy 2025?

options.text: Importing partially processed steel and finishing it domestically qualifies as “domestic”
Steel exports must include documentation of Indian melting processes
Steel used in government-funded projects is completely manufactured in India
Biometric authentication is required at smelting plants for traceability

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel used in government-funded projects is completely manufactured in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Melt and Pour’ rule:** This rule mandates that steel used for **government-funded projects** must be completely manufactured in **India**. It ensures that the steel is melted, poured, and processed entirely within the country.
 
• The rule aims to enhance the usage of domestically produced steel and supports the vision of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (self-reliant India), reducing dependency on imported steel. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• This provision is part of the **Domestically Manufactured Iron & Steel Products (DMI&SP) Policy 2025**, which seeks to promote the domestic steel industry and ensure the quality of steel used in critical projects.
 
• The rule prevents practices such as importing partially processed steel and finishing it domestically to classify it as "domestic." Instead, it strictly requires complete domestic production. *Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Documentation of Indian melting processes for exports is not a requirement under the ‘Melt and Pour’ rule, making *Option 2 incorrect.*
 
• Biometric authentication at smelting plants is not a part of this rule, which makes *Option 4 incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Domestically Manufactured Iron & Steel Products (DMI&SP) Policy:**

 
 
• The **DMI&SP Policy** was introduced by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, to ensure the use of domestically produced steel in government-funded projects.
 
• This policy contributes to the growth of the **Indian steel industry**, which plays a critical role in infrastructure development, manufacturing, and economic growth.
 
• The policy aligns with the government’s **Make in India** initiative, ensuring that domestic industries benefit from government procurement.
 
 
 
• **Features of the ‘Melt and Pour’ Rule:**
 
 
• It establishes strict guidelines for steel production processes, ensuring that the steel used in government projects is melted and poured in **India**.
 
• This prevents the misuse of classifications and guarantees the authenticity of domestically manufactured steel.
 
• The rule helps maintain **quality standards** and boosts the competitiveness of Indian steel manufacturers.
 
 
 
• **Applications of the DMI&SP Policy:**
 
 
• The policy is applicable to government-funded projects, including infrastructure projects such as highways, bridges, railways, and power plants.
 
• It promotes the use of domestic steel in sectors like **construction**, **defense**, and **energy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Steel Industry:**

 
 
• India is the **second-largest steel producer** in the world, with an annual production capacity exceeding **100 million tonnes**.
 
• The industry contributes significantly to the country’s **GDP** and provides employment to millions.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government has launched initiatives like **National Steel Policy 2017** to enhance production capacity and support sustainable practices.
 
• The DMI&SP Policy is a vital part of these efforts, ensuring the growth and competitiveness of the domestic steel industry.

questions.question: Which important Sikh festival is on 5 November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Nanak Jayanti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Nanak Jayanti**, also known as **Gurpurab**, commemorates the birth anniversary of **Guru Nanak Dev**, the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism.
 
• Guru Nanak Jayanti is celebrated on the day of **Kartik Purnima** according to the Hindu lunar calendar, which usually falls in the month of **November**. In **2025**, it is observed on **5th November**.
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji** was born in **1469** in **Nankana Sahib**, located in present-day **Pakistan**. His teachings emphasized **unity, equality, selfless service, and devotion to God**.
 
• The celebrations typically begin with **Akhand Path**, a continuous reading of the **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of Sikhism, for 48 hours.
 
• A day before Guru Nanak Jayanti, a procession known as **Nagar Kirtan** is held, where devotees sing hymns and carry the Sikh flag, **Nishan Sahib**.
 
• On the day of the festival, Sikhs visit **Gurdwaras** and participate in prayers, kirtans, and community meals called **Langar**. The Langar reflects the values of **equality and selfless service**.
 
• The festival is not only celebrated by Sikhs but also revered by people of other communities who follow Guru Nanak Dev Ji's teachings of universal brotherhood and peace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Teachings:**

 
 
• **Equality:** Guru Nanak Dev Ji rejected caste discrimination and emphasized that all humans are equal, irrespective of their religion, caste, or gender.
 
• **Selfless Service:** He encouraged people to engage in community service and help the needy without expecting anything in return.
 
• **Three Pillars:** Guru Nanak Dev Ji propagated three principles: **Naam Japo** (meditate on God’s name), **Kirat Karo** (earn an honest living), and **Vand Chakko** (share with others).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Langar:**
 
 
• The concept of Langar involves serving free meals to everyone, irrespective of their religion, caste, or social status. It is a symbol of **community service** and **equality**.
 
• Langar was initiated by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and has become an integral part of Sikhism.
 
 
 
• **Celebrations Across the Globe:**
 
 
• Guru Nanak Jayanti is celebrated worldwide by Sikhs and others who follow his teachings, especially in countries like **India, Pakistan, Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom**.
 
• Special arrangements are made at **Gurdwaras** globally to mark this auspicious occasion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Sikh Festivals:**

 
 
• **Baisakhi:** Celebrated in April, marking the harvest season and the founding of the **Khalsa Panth** by Guru Gobind Singh Ji in **1699**.
 
• **Lohri:** Celebrated in January, especially in Punjab, marking the harvest of winter crops and the beginning of the harvest season.
 
• **Holi:** Though primarily a Hindu festival celebrated in March, Sikhs also celebrate it as **Hola Mohalla**, a tradition established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings laid the foundation of **Sikhism**, which emphasizes the importance of **spirituality, moral values, and social equality**.
 
• His legacy continues to inspire millions worldwide, promoting **peace, harmony, and universal brotherhood**.

questions.question: Which Indian space tech startup along with Google launched India's first private satellite constellation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pixxel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pixxel** is an Indian space technology startup focused on building a constellation of advanced earth imaging satellites. The company's primary goal is to provide high-resolution hyperspectral data for various applications.
 
• Pixxel, in collaboration with **Google**, launched **India's first private satellite constellation**. This marked a significant milestone in India's private space sector.
 
• The collaboration with Google enabled Pixxel to leverage advanced analytics and cloud computing platforms to process the data collected by their satellites. This partnership highlights the importance of integrating technology and space science. *Hence, Pixxel is the correct option.*
 
• Pixxel's satellite constellation aims to provide critical insights into various sectors, such as agriculture, climate monitoring, and natural disaster management, by offering real-time data and analytics.
 
• This achievement aligns with the Indian government's efforts to promote private participation in space exploration, fostering innovation and global collaboration. *Hence, Pixxel's contribution is significant for India's space industry.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Pixxel:**

 
 
• Pixxel is a **Bengaluru-based space tech startup** founded in **2019**. It aims to build a constellation of satellites for high-resolution imagery.
 
• Pixxel's focus is on **hyperspectral imaging**, which provides detailed data by capturing images in multiple wavelengths of the light spectrum.
 
• The company launched its first satellite, **Anand**, in **April 2022** as part of its mission to deploy a network of satellites for real-time earth observation.
 
 
 
• **Role of Google in the Partnership:**
 
 
• Google partnered with Pixxel to provide **cloud computing and AI-powered analytics** solutions for processing satellite data.
 
• The collaboration allows Pixxel to utilize **Google Cloud's AI and machine learning tools** to analyze hyperspectral data effectively and deliver actionable insights to various industries.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Pixxel's Satellite Constellation:**
 
 
• **Agriculture:** Monitoring crop health, soil quality, and water resources to optimize farming practices.
 
• **Environmental monitoring:** Tracking deforestation, pollution, and climate change impact to ensure ecological sustainability.
 
• **Disaster management:** Providing real-time data to predict and mitigate the impact of natural disasters like floods, droughts, and wildfires.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Private Satellite Constellations:**

 
 
• **Private companies**, such as Pixxel, are playing a crucial role in advancing space technology and making high-resolution satellite data accessible to industries and governments.
 
• The involvement of private players in space exploration aligns with the Indian government's **space policy reforms**, encouraging innovation and global competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Other Startups in Indian Space Tech:**
 
 
• **Skyroot Aerospace:** Focused on developing cost-effective and reliable launch vehicles for small satellites.
 
• **AgniKul Cosmos:** Specializes in building customizable launch vehicles for low-earth orbit satellites.
 
• **Bellatrix Aerospace:** Working on developing in-space propulsion systems and orbital launch vehicles.

questions.question: The government initiative known as KIRTI, an acronym for Khelo India Rising Talent Identification, was inaugurated in ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **KIRTI** stands for **Khelo India Rising Talent Identification**. It is an initiative launched by the Government of India to identify and nurture young sports talent across the country.
 
• The primary goal of **KIRTI** is to promote sports culture and provide a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent at the national and international level.
 
• The initiative was officially launched in the year **2024**. *Hence, the correct answer is 2024.*
 
• **KIRTI** aims to bridge the gap in sports infrastructure and provide necessary resources like training, coaching, and facilities to aspiring athletes in India.
 
• This initiative is a part of the broader **Khelo India Programme**, which was launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to encourage sports participation and the overall development of sports in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Programme:**

 
 
• Launched in **2018**, this programme is a flagship scheme of the Government of India to revive the sports culture in India at the grassroot level.
 
• Under this programme, talented players are identified in various sports disciplines and provided with financial assistance of **₹5 lakh annually** for a period of 8 years.
 
• The programme has successfully organized events like the **Khelo India Youth Games** and **Khelo India University Games**, which have become a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of KIRTI:**
 
 
• To identify young sports talent from schools, colleges, and various sports competitions across India and provide them with the required resources.
 
• To develop a strong network of sports infrastructure in both urban and rural areas to ensure accessibility for everyone.
 
• To create an ecosystem that encourages sports as a career option and elevates India’s performance on international platforms such as the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of KIRTI:**
 
 
• Focuses on grassroots-level talent identification and development.
 
• Encourages collaboration between the government, private sector, and sports federations for better results.
 
• Offers access to world-class coaching facilities and training under expert coaches to enhance athletes' performance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Sports in Nation Building:**

 
 
• Sports play a significant role in fostering a sense of unity, discipline, and national pride. Initiatives like **KIRTI** help in identifying young talent and empowering them to represent the country at the global level.
 
• Such programmes contribute to the physical and mental well-being of individuals and help address issues like obesity and lifestyle diseases through increased participation in physical activities.
 
 
 
• **Major Sports Achievements of India:**
 
 
• **Olympics:** India has seen a steady rise in its medal tally in recent Olympics, with notable performances in sports like weightlifting, wrestling, and badminton.
 
• **Cricket:** India has won the ICC Cricket World Cup twice (in **1983** and **2011**), along with several other cricketing milestones.
 
• **Paralympics:** Indian athletes have excelled in the Paralympics, with remarkable performances in events like javelin throw, high jump, and badminton.

questions.question: Which Indian city was announced by the global governing body WPA as the host of the 2025 Para Athletics World Championships?

__
 
• The **2025 Para Athletics World Championships** will be hosted by **New Delhi**, India. This marks the first time India will host this prestigious international event.
 
• The announcement was made by the **World Para Athletics (WPA)**, the global governing body for para-athletics, highlighting India’s growing focus on promoting sports for differently-abled athletes.
 
• India has previously hosted significant para-sporting events, including the **Commonwealth Games** and the **Asian Para Games**, which reflects its capability in organizing global tournaments. *Hence, New Delhi is the correct location for hosting the event.*
 
• **New Delhi**, the capital city of India, is well-equipped with world-class facilities, infrastructure, and accessibility standards required for hosting such a major international para-athletics event.
 
• The event is expected to attract athletes from all over the world, promoting ** in sports and showcasing India's organizational capabilities. *Hence, New Delhi is a strategic choice for the venue.*
 
• India’s hosting of the Para Athletics World Championships** aligns with its commitment to empowering differently-abled individuals and fostering a culture of equality in sports. **Para-sports** have gained significant attention in India over the past decade. *Hence, the announcement is a milestone in India’s sporting history.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About World Para Athletics:**

 
 
• **World Para Athletics (WPA)** is the governing body for para-athletics worldwide. It is a part of the **International Paralympic Committee (IPC)**, which oversees various para-sporting events globally.
 
• WPA organizes several international events, including **World Championships**, which provide a platform for athletes with disabilities to showcase their talents and compete at the highest level.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi as a Sporting Hub:**
 
 
• **New Delhi** is known for hosting several international sporting events, such as the **2010 Commonwealth Games**, showcasing its infrastructure and organizational capabilities.
 
• The city is equipped with facilities like the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** and **Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium**, which are among the largest and most advanced stadiums in India.
 
• The city is well-connected internationally and domestically, making it a convenient location for athletes and officials traveling from across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Para Athletics World Championships:**
 
 
• The **Para Athletics World Championships** serves as a platform for promoting inclusivity and accessibility in sports, encouraging the participation of differently-abled athletes.
 
• The event helps in breaking societal barriers and stereotypes associated with disability, fostering a spirit of equality and empowerment.
 
• It also highlights the importance of infrastructure development and policy-making to support para-athletes in their training and competitions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Achievements in Para Sports:**

 
 
• India has shown remarkable progress in **para-sports** over the years, with athletes winning accolades in events such as the **Paralympic Games**, **Asian Para Games**, and various international championships.
 
• Prominent Indian para-athletes like **Devendra Jhajharia** (javelin throw) and **Deepa Malik** (shot put) have won medals in global events, inspiring many across the nation.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Para Sports:**
 
 
• The Indian government has introduced several schemes to support para-athletes, including the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** and **Para Sports Development Fund**.
 
• The **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** plays a crucial role in providing training facilities, coaching, and financial assistance to para-athletes.
 
• India’s hosting of the 2025 Para Athletics World Championships is an important step in furthering its commitment to promoting para-sports on the global stage.
